items.readable_text:
Content:
For a general logarithm of base [MATH: a,] the derivative is given by

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{ \textrm{d} x}\left( \log_a x \right)= \dfrac{1}{x\ln a}.]

Content:
Also, recall that whenever [MATH: \log] is written without a base, we can assume that it represents the base [MATH: 10.] So, we have

Content:
[MATH: \log x = \log_{10} x.]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(\log x)|= (d)/(dx)(\log_{10} x) = (1)/(x\ln 10).]

Content:
Note: To see where this rule comes from, we can use the change-of-base formula as shown below.
[MATH: \log_a x = \dfrac{\ln x}{\ln a}]

Content:
Taking the derivative and using the fact that [MATH: \ln a] is a constant, then, we have

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(\log_{a} x)|= (d)/(dx)((\ln x)/(\ln a)); = (1)/(\ln a) ⋅ (d)/(dx)(\ln x); = (1)/(\ln a) ⋅ (1)/(x); = (1)/(x\ln a).]

key_prerequisites.name: Calculating the Slope of a Tangent Line Using Differentiation

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: y= \log_4 x + \ln x], find the slope of the tangent at [MATH: x=1.]
sections.readable_text: Given that [MATH: y= \log_4 x + \ln x], find the slope of the tangent at [MATH: x=1.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find [MATH: \dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}] at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have [MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( \log_4 x + \ln x \right)\ &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\log_4 x) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\ln x )\ &= \dfrac{1}{x\ln 4} + \dfrac{1}{x}. }]

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at [MATH: x=1] is

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|_{x = 1}|= ((1)/(x\ln 4) + (1)/(x))|_{x = 1}; = (1)/(\ln 4) + 1.]

items.readable_text:
Example Prompt:

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find [MATH: \dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}] at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}
&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( \log_4 x + \ln x \right)\
&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\log_4 x) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\ln x )\
&= \dfrac{1}{x\ln 4} + \dfrac{1}{x}.
}]

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at [MATH: x=1] is

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|_{x = 1}|= ((1)/(x\ln 4) + (1)/(x))|_{x = 1}; = (1)/(\ln 4) + 1.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function with a General Base

Content:
For a general logarithm of base [MATH: a,] the derivative is given by

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{ \textrm{d} x}\left( \log_a x \right)= \dfrac{1}{x\ln a}.]

Content:
Also, recall that whenever [MATH: \log] is written without a base, we can assume that it represents the base [MATH: 10.] So, we have

Content:
[MATH: \log x = \log_{10} x.]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(\log x)|= (d)/(dx)(\log_{10} x) = (1)/(x\ln 10).]

Content:
Note: To see where this rule comes from, we can use the change-of-base formula as shown below.
[MATH: \log_a x = \dfrac{\ln x}{\ln a}]

Content:
Taking the derivative and using the fact that [MATH: \ln a] is a constant, then, we have

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(\log_{a} x)|= (d)/(dx)((\ln x)/(\ln a)); = (1)/(\ln a) ⋅ (d)/(dx)(\ln x); = (1)/(\ln a) ⋅ (1)/(x); = (1)/(x\ln a).]
